validated_work_order.understanding: Posting a scheduled transaction and then moving that transaction's date to an earlier day makes the schedule reappear as an un-posted row in the transactions table and flips its status from 'Paid' back to 'Due'. Root mechanism: whether an occurrence counts as paid is derived from a DATE COMPARISON around schedule.next_date, not from the existence of a transaction linked to that schedule. getScheduleOccurrenceMatchStartDate returns next_date itself as the lower bound whenever the date condition op is 'is' (packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts:95-97), getHasTransactionsQuery then selects only transactions with schedule = <id> AND date >= that bound (schedules.ts:165-193), and isScheduleOccurrencePosted applies the same lower bound plus an upper bound of occurrenceDate (schedules.ts:130-152). Posting creates the transaction dated exactly next_date, so it matches. Editing the date to any earlier day moves it below the lower bound, the query stops matching, hasTrans goes false, getStatus falls back to comparing next_date with today and returns 'due' (schedules.ts:52-76), and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions regenerates the schedule row because 'due' is in the isForPreview list (schedules.ts:425-434). The transaction stays linked to the schedule throughout; only the date comparison changed. I reproduced this myself against http://localhost:3001 today (2026-10-02): posted 'Phone bills' (Dominion Power, Bank of America, 120.00, date condition op 'is' monthly on the 2nd) from the Schedules page, which set the status to 'Paid' and created the transaction dated 10/02/2026; then re-dated that transaction to 09/25/2026, SEVEN days early, and the register brought the schedule row straight back, reading '10/02/2026 | Dominion Power | Phone bills | Due | 120.00', while the Schedules page flipped that row from 'Paid' to 'Due'. No console errors or page errors were emitted at any step. THE REJECTED PLAN (v2) proposed the window (previousOccurrence, occurrenceDate], keeping exact-date matching when the date condition has no preceding occurrence. I confirmed by execution that this fails on the very fixture it ships: the demo schedule's recurrence STARTS at currentDay() (mocks/budget.ts:969 creates {start: currentDay(), frequency: 'monthly'}), so next_date IS the first occurrence, the reverse lookup returns an empty array, and the plan falls back to exact-date matching - leaving AC-1 and AC-2 unable to pass. I also confirmed its own probe line 'occ=2026-10-02 prev=2026-09-02' is unreachable for that fixture.
validated_work_order.root_cause: Whether a schedule occurrence counts as paid is derived from a date comparison around schedule.next_date rather than from the existence of a transaction linked to that schedule. getScheduleOccurrenceMatchStartDate returns next_date itself as the lower bound whenever the date condition op is 'is' (schedules.ts:95-97), and both callers then require the linked transaction to be dated on or after that bound (getHasTransactionsQuery at schedules.ts:165-193, isScheduleOccurrencePosted at schedules.ts:130-152). Posting creates the transaction dated exactly next_date, so it matches and the status becomes 'paid'; editing that transaction's date to any earlier day moves it below the bound, the same query stops matching it, hasTrans goes false, getStatus falls back to comparing next_date with today, and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions regenerates the schedule row. The lower bound is the wrong SHAPE for the problem: the gap between next_date and the real payment date is a property of how early the user paid, not a constant, and it is bounded above only by the schedule's own recurrence interval.
validated_work_order.approach: Derive the lower bound from the schedule's own recurrence INTERVAL rather than from the existence of a preceding occurrence. For a recurring schedule, the match window for occurrence D becomes [previousOccurrence(D) + 1 day, D] - the day after the previous occurrence through D itself. Because the previous occurrence is computed from a copy of the recurrence whose start is shifted back exactly one interval, the bound is available even when D is the FIRST occurrence of the series (the demo fixture, and every schedule a user creates today), which is exactly what the rejected plan could not do. Two properties make this the correct shape: the window is as wide as the schedule's own recurrence cycle, so it covers an early payment of any size the reporter's scenario can produce; and consecutive occurrences produce disjoint windows, so one transaction can satisfy at most one occurrence. Measured disjointness for the demo monthly series: [2026-09-03,2026-10-02] [2026-10-03,2026-11-02] [2026-11-03,2026-12-02]; a transaction dated 2026-10-15 satisfies exactly ['2026-11-02'], and 2026-09-25 satisfies exactly ['2026-10-02']. Measured daily: occurrence 2024-03-10 gets lower bound 2024-03-10 and 2024-03-11 gets 2024-03-11, i.e. ZERO widening, so a daily schedule cannot double-count. Implementation notes that are load-bearing and were each measured: (1) compute the shifted start with date-fns d.subDays/d.subWeeks/d.subMonths/d.subYears and format the result back to 'yyyy-MM-dd' - do NOT use monthUtils.subMonths, which formats to 'yyyy-MM' and SILENTLY DROPS THE DAY, turning a 2026-10-02 occurrence into a 2026-09-01 bound and over-widening the window by a day; (2) honour the config's interval (default 1) so an every-2-months schedule gets a 2-month bound - measured 2024-05-10 -> 2024-03-11; (3) look the previous occurrence up with the same reverse RSchedule iteration getNextDate already uses, driven from the shifted start, bounded to dates strictly before D. Keep exact-date matching for auto-posted schedules (posts_transaction true), for one-time schedules (string date value), and for any date condition the recurrence cannot produce an interval for; keep the existing 2-day lookback for schedules with no date condition at all. Keep the helper as the single seam so all three callers get the fix together, and keep the returned bound INCLUSIVE, because getHasTransactionsQuery uses $gte and isScheduleOccurrencePosted uses >= - returning previousOccurrence + 1 day preserves both without touching either caller.

files.change: In getScheduleOccurrenceMatchStartDate (currently lines 90-102), replace the bare `return occurrenceDate` short-circuit in the `dateCond?.op === 'is'` branch with a recurrence-derived lower bound. Add a small module-level helper that, given the date condition value and an occurrence date D: returns D unchanged when the value is a string (one-time schedule); otherwise computes a shifted start by subtracting exactly one recurrence interval from value.start using date-fns (d.subDays / d.subWeeks / d.subMonths / d.subYears, honouring value.interval ?? 1) and formatting back to 'yyyy-MM-dd' - it must NOT use monthUtils.subMonths, which formats to 'yyyy-MM' and silently drops the day; then builds a Condition with op 'is' over {...value, start: shiftedStart} exactly as getNextDate does, takes the last occurrence strictly before D via value.schedule.occurrences({ start, end: addDays(D,-1), reverse: true, take: 1 }), and returns addDays(thatOccurrence, 1). If the frequency is unrecognised or the recurrence yields no previous occurrence, fall back to the current exact `return occurrenceDate`. Return the bound INCLUSIVE so the existing `$gte` in getHasTransactionsQuery and `>=` in isScheduleOccurrencePosted need no change. Keep the posts_transaction short-circuit and the trailing 2-day lookback for schedules with no date condition exactly as they are. Update the doc comment above getScheduleOccurrenceMatchStartDate AND the equivalent comment above getHasTransactionsQuery (lines 154-164), which currently states '`dateCond.op === "is"` (one-time or recurring): exact `next_date`, no lookback', to state the corrected contract: the lower bound is the day after the schedule's previous occurrence, so a bill paid any time within its recurrence cycle satisfies the occurrence it belongs to, and consecutive occurrences therefore get disjoint windows so one transaction can satisfy at most one.
files.why: This single helper is the lower bound for all three callers (getHasTransactionsQuery in useSchedules and advanceSchedulesService, and isScheduleOccurrencePosted in forecast-schedules). Deriving the bound from the recurrence interval rather than from the existence of a preceding occurrence is what makes it work for the demo fixture and for any schedule whose series starts at its first occurrence - the specific reason the previous plan could not pass its own acceptance criteria.

qa_script: 1. `yarn start`, open $PREVIEW_URL, click 'Try the demo' on the welcome screen. This creates a 'Phone bills' schedule: Dominion Power, Bank of America, monthly on the 2nd, date condition op 'is', posts_transaction false, recurrence start EQUALS today so next_date is the series' FIRST occurrence (created by packages/loot-core/src/mocks/budget.ts:966-975). That first-occurrence property is the point: the rejected plan's fix does nothing for this fixture.
2. Go to Schedules. Confirm 'Phone bills' reads: Dominion Power | Bank of America | 10/02/2026 | Due | 120.00.
3. Right-click 'Phone bills' and choose 'Post transaction'. Confirm the Schedules page now shows status 'Paid' and that the Bank of America register no longer shows the 'Phone bills' schedule row.
4. Open Bank of America. The posted transaction reads 10/02/2026 | Dominion Power | Categorize | 120.00.

5. Click that transaction's date cell, navigate back one month, and pick a date SEVEN DAYS before the original due date (09/25/2026). This is the reproduced gap, well beyond the two days the rejected plan assumed.

6. THE BUG, before the fix: the schedule row reappears in the register as '10/02/2026 | Dominion Power | Phone bills | Due | 120.00' and the Schedules page flips from 'Paid' to 'Due'. After the fix, neither happens: the register shows only the posted transaction and the Schedules page still reads 'Paid'. Reload the page and confirm it stays 'Paid'.

7. Future-due variant, the reporter's own shape, landing STRICTLY INSIDE the window: back on Schedules, right-click 'Phone bills' > 'Skip next scheduled date' so next_date moves to 11/02/2026 (a ~31-day gap), post it, then re-date the posted transaction to a date inside the window - 10/20/2026, eighteen days early, which is after the previous occurrence 10/02/2026. The status must remain 'Paid' and no schedule row may reappear. Do NOT use 10/02/2026 here: that is the previous occurrence's own date and is the deliberately excluded boundary stated in AC-3.

8. Regression sweep: on the Schedules page, 'Skip next scheduled date' and 'Post transaction today' must still behave as before; an auto-posted schedule (created with 'Automatically add transaction' enabled) must still match on its exact date; and a forecast for an account with a re-dated scheduled transaction must not double-count the bill - confirm one daily recurring schedule paid once still projects its later occurrences.
risks: ONE PRODUCT CALL REMAINS, now scoped rather than deferred: a payment dated EXACTLY on the previous occurrence's own date is not matched by the later occurrence. The demo fixture makes this reachable - skip next_date to 11/02/2026 and re-date the transaction to 10/02/2026 does not stay Paid. This is stated inside AC-3 with the reason (closing the window would double-count, measured), and qa_script step 7 deliberately uses 10/20/2026 instead. If a maintainer wants that boundary covered, it needs a different mechanism, not a wider window.

Deriving the lower bound requires building a Condition and reverse-iterating the recurrence per schedule, where the current code is a constant-time branch. getHasTransactionsQuery maps over all schedules and isScheduleOccurrencePosted runs per occurrence, so this is a real change in cost profile and is the one thing I did not measure at scale. The iteration is bounded (reverse, take: 1) and rule objects are already constructed elsewhere in the same paths.

packages/loot-core/src/server/forecast/ has NO test file for forecast-schedules, so the forecast path - one of the three callers - is currently untested. The new forecast-schedules.test.ts is load-bearing for AC-5, not optional, and the previous plan's reliance on 'the existing suite will catch it' proved nothing.

advanceSchedulesService reads the same status and WRITES to the database by advancing next_date. A window that were too wide could advance a recurring schedule past an occurrence that was never paid, permanently skipping a bill. The disjointness property is what makes this safe and AC-5 requires it to be asserted by a test rather than assumed.

Auto-posted schedules deliberately keep the exact-date bound, so their behaviour is unchanged. But if an implementer widens the window for posts_transaction schedules as well, a genuinely missed occurrence could be treated as paid and never auto-posted. The posts_transaction cases in AC-6 must stay on exact matching.

The date-condition value can carry several shapes (string, monthly with day patterns producing two rules, endMode after_n_occurrences or on_date, interval > 1, skipWeekend). All the ones I could construct were measured and resolve correctly, but skipWeekend shifts an occurrence onto a different day AFTER the recurrence is computed, so a weekend-solved occurrence may not line up exactly with a raw recurrence occurrence. I did not test skipWeekend and the implementer should add a case for it rather than assume.

packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts is marked `// @ts-strict-ignore`. New code there inherits that; do not add the marker to any NEW file and do not remove the existing one as part of this change.
out_of_scope: Whether posting a schedule whose due date is in the future should advance next_date at all is a separate design question. advanceSchedulesService only reaches its setNextDate branch for schedules already computed as 'paid' (packages/loot-core/src/server/schedules/app.ts:747-762); this change does not restructure that service.

The excluded exact-boundary case (payment dated exactly on the previous occurrence's date) is out of scope by design and is documented in AC-3. Covering it needs a stamp recording which occurrence a transaction was posted from, not a wider window.

evidence: REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY against http://localhost:3001 (Chromium, fresh session, demo budget). Today is 2026-10-02. No console errors and no page errors were emitted at any step.

Setup: 'Phone bills' in the demo budget is the reporter's shape - payee Dominion Power, account Bank of America, posts_transaction false, date condition { op: 'is', value: { start: currentDay(), frequency: 'monthly', patterns: [], skipWeekend: false, weekendSolveMode: 'after' } } (packages/loot-core/src/mocks/budget.ts:950-975).
Schedules page before posting: 'Phone bills | Dominion Power | Bank of America | 10/02/2026 | Due | ~ | 120.00'.
After 'Post transaction': status becomes 'Paid', and the register correctly drops the schedule row, showing '10/02/2026 | Dominion Power | Categorize | 120.00'.

THE BUG, after clicking the posted transaction's date cell, navigating back one month and picking 09/25/2026 (SEVEN days early): the register shows the schedule row back alongside the real transaction - '10/03/2026 | (No payee) | Utilities | Upcoming | 1,900.00 / 10/02/2026 | Dominion Power | Phone bills | Due | 120.00  <-- resurrected / 10/01/2026 | Fast Internet | Internet bill | Missed | 140.00 / 10/02/2026 | Dominion Power | Categorize | 120.00  <-- the real, linked transaction' - and the Schedules page row for 'Phone bills' flips from 'Paid' to 'Due'.

OBJECTION 1 CONFIRMED BY EXECUTION. Running the real Condition/RSchedule pipeline against the demo fixture: an unshifted reverse lookup for occurrences strictly before 2026-10-02 returns [] (an empty array) - the series has no preceding occurrence. The rejected plan keeps exact-date matching in exactly that case, so for the fixture it ships, its fix returns the occurrence date unchanged and the reproduced bug survives. Its own probe line 'occ=2026-10-02 prev=2026-09-02' is unreachable for this fixture.

Corrected fix shape validated on the demo fixture itself (start === next_date === 2026-10-02, shifted start 2026-09-02): lower bound 2026-09-03; a payment dated 2026-09-25 is inside the window; end-to-end getStatus returns 'paid' and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions returns 0 preview rows.

MEASURED DAILY (the AC-5 guard): occurrence 2024-03-10 -> bound 2024-03-10, occurrence 2024-03-11 -> bound 2024-03-11, i.e. zero widening; a transaction dated 2024-03-10 satisfies 2024-03-10 and NOT 2024-03-11.

OBJECTION 2 RESOLVED, NOT RESTATED. The reviewer's preferred alternative - closing the window on both ends - was implemented and measured: it double-counts. With both ends closed, a transaction dated 2026-10-02 satisfies ['2026-10-02','2026-11-02'] and a transaction dated 2026-11-02 satisfies ['2026-11-02','2026-12-02']. The reason is structural: posting creates the transaction dated EXACTLY next_date, so the window's right end must remain closed, and closing the left end too makes adjacent windows share a boundary date. The half-open left end is therefore the only self-consistent reading, so AC-3 is restated to the cases the fix genuinely covers with the limitation in the criterion text.

MEASURED with the corrected bound on the reporter's future-due variant: occurrence 2026-11-02 -> bound 2026-10-03; a payment dated 2026-10-20 returns status 'paid'; a payment dated 2026-10-02, exactly the previous occurrence's date, returns 'scheduled' - the excluded boundary, now stated inside AC-3 instead of being deferred.

MEASURED day-loss trap: monthUtils.subMonths(P('2026-10-02'), 1) returns '2026-09-01' because it formats to 'yyyy-MM' and drops the day, while date-fns subMonths preserves 2026-09-02. Using monthUtils.subMonths would over-widen every monthly window by a day and re-introduce boundary overlap; the work order requires date-fns and adds a regression case.

MEASURED interval handling: an every-2-months monthly schedule (start 2024-01-10) returns bound 2024-03-11 for occurrence 2024-05-10, so a first-occurrence schedule with interval > 1 still gets a widened window.

MEASURED month-end clamping follows the SERIES, not arithmetic: a monthly-on-the-31st recurrence (start 2024-01-31) has occurrences 2024-01-31 and 2024-03-31 (February has no 31st and is skipped), so the bound for occurrence 2024-03-31 is 2024-02-01 - derived from the real previous occurrence 2024-01-31, not the arithmetically-implied 2024-03-01.

MEASURED endMode and pattern edges, all resolving without throwing: after_n_occurrences (occurrence 2024-03-10 -> 2024-02-11), on_date (occurrence 2024-06-10 -> 2024-05-11), monthly restricted to the 15th (occurrence 2024-04-15 -> 2024-03-16), weekly first occurrence (occurrence 2024-01-10 -> 2024-01-04), daily first occurrence (2026-10-02 -> 2026-10-02).

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep the previous plan's (previousOccurrence, occurrenceDate] window, but only widen when a preceding occurrence exists, and change the QA fixture to create the schedule with a start in a prior month.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This is the review's objection-1 option (b). It makes the demo fixture pass by editing the test rather than the product, and it explicitly scopes out a next_date that is the series' first occurrence - which is exactly what every schedule a user creates today produces, and exactly the reporter's fixture. It fixes the reproduction I watched rather than the bug.

alternatives_considered.approach: Close the match window on BOTH ends, so a payment dated exactly on the previous occurrence's date counts toward the later occurrence too (the review's objection-2 option (a)).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Measured to double-count. Because posting creates the transaction dated exactly next_date, the window's right end must stay closed; closing the left end as well makes adjacent windows share their boundary. A transaction dated 2026-10-02 then satisfies both ['2026-10-02','2026-11-02'] and the forecast suppresses a bill that was never paid, which is worse than the bug being fixed. The half-open left end is the only self-consistent reading.

alternatives_considered.approach: Record the occurrence a transaction was posted from (e.g. a scheduleId + occurrence stamp on the transaction) and match on that instead of on dates.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It is the most semantically correct design - it makes the half-open boundary debate moot - but it requires a schema/migration change to the transactions table and touches every write path that can create or move a schedule-linked transaction. Far beyond a bug fix, and the implementer could not land it inside this ticket's review budget.

alternatives_considered.approach: Make the window symmetric around the occurrence date, or use a constant scaled by frequency (e.g. monthly -> 31 days) instead of the true previous occurrence.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: A symmetric window overlaps its neighbour by construction and double-counts. A constant scaled by frequency is not disjoint for month-end recurrences (a monthly-on-the-31st schedule skips February, so consecutive occurrences are two months apart while the constant assumes one) and it repeats the class of bug the previous plan was rejected for - a bound unrelated to the actual recurrence.

alternatives_considered.approach: Suppress the preview row purely because a linked transaction exists at any date, ignoring the date comparison entirely.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It would let a transaction from six months ago mark today's occurrence paid, so a genuinely unpaid bill would never be projected or re-posted. That is the old-transaction guard the code comments explicitly warn about, and the disjoint window is what prevents it.

assumptions: monthUtils.currentDay() is driven by MockDate/setup in the loot-core vitest environment (measured: tests pinned to 2017-01-01), so tests asserting behaviour around 'today' must set MockDate explicitly rather than rely on the system clock.
packages/loot-core/vitest.config.ts suppresses stdout console logs via onConsoleLog, so any test that needs to print diagnostics must run with --disable-console-intercept.

The $PREVIEW_URL app on this runner is the standard demo budget and the browser session is disposable; the reproduction created only schedule-posting state that the demo regenerates, so no cleanup of user records was needed.

A Condition can be constructed from a date-condition value directly inside packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts without creating an import cycle, since getNextDate and scheduleIsRecurring in the same file already do exactly this.
unknowns: How the product should behave when a payment lands exactly on the previous occurrence's date. I proved a date-window fix cannot cover it without double-counting, but whether the right answer is 'treat as unpaid' (current), 'treat as paid for the later occurrence', or 'ask the user' is a product decision outside this ticket.

How skipWeekend interacts with a recurrence-derived bound. getNextDate applies getDateWithSkippedWeekend AFTER the recurrence resolves, so a weekend-solved next_date may not correspond to a raw occurrence date; I did not test this case.
The per-schedule cost of constructing a Condition and reverse-iterating the recurrence. The iteration is bounded (reverse, take: 1) but I did not measure it against a large budget's schedule count.

Whether monthly schedules with BOTH day-of-month and day-of-week patterns (which recurConfigToRSchedule expands into two separate rrules) resolve to a single unambiguous previous occurrence, or whether the helper should union both rules' occurrences.
validated_work_order.debate_summary: The v2 plan was rejected on two grounds and I reproduced both objections rather than arguing with them. Objection 1 (AC-1/AC-2 cannot pass on the shipped fixture) is CORRECT and I confirmed it by execution: the demo recurrence starts AT next_date, so v2's 'no preceding occurrence -> exact date' fallback leaves the reproduced case exactly as broken, and its own probe line was unreachable. I answered it with option (a) the reviewer offered: derive the bound from the recurrence INTERVAL, not from the existence of a preceding occurrence, so a first-occurrence next_date still gets a widened window. Validated on the exact demo fixture: bound 2026-09-03, a 7-day-early payment lands inside, getStatus returns 'paid', preview rows 0. Objection 2 (AC-3 is a criterion the approach provably fails) is also CORRECT, and I went further than restating it: I proved the reviewer's preferred alternative - closing the window on both ends - is itself impossible, because posting creates a transaction dated EXACTLY next_date, so the window's right end must stay closed, and closing the left end too makes windows share their boundary date. Measured: with both ends closed, a transaction dated 2026-10-02 satisfies BOTH ['2026-10-02','2026-11-02'] - a real double count that would break AC-5 in the forecast. The half-open left end is therefore the only self-consistent reading, so I restated AC-3 to the boundary cases the fix genuinely covers and moved the exact-boundary limitation out of residual_risks and INTO the criterion's own text, which is what the reviewer asked for. I also corrected a factual claim carried over from v2: it asserted the two existing tests at schedules.test.ts:337-361 do not encode the bug and need no deletion. By execution they DO change - monthly-with-start-equal-to-occurrence moves from 2024-03-10 to 2024-02-11, and the isScheduleOccurrencePosted case 'early pay day before due for recurring date cond' flips from false to true - so the work order now names both explicitly as tests to update rather than leave to the implementer.
residual_risks: skipWeekend is the one date-condition feature I could not exercise; a weekend-solved next_date may not align with a raw recurrence occurrence and could yield a subtly wrong bound. The implementer should add an explicit skipWeekend case rather than assume the general path covers it.
The recurrence lookup is a new per-schedule cost in getHasTransactionsQuery, which maps over all schedules on every status refresh; bounded (reverse, take 1) but unmeasured at scale.
Monthly schedules carrying day-of-week patterns expand to two rrules via recurConfigToRSchedule; whether the helper unions both rules' occurrences correctly is untested.

advanceSchedulesService writes next_date based on this status, so a wrongly widened window could permanently skip an unpaid bill. AC-5's disjointness test is the guard against this and is mandatory, not optional.
